We also describe a generalization of the Mellin space formalism which incorporates the compact momentum, and we discuss some possible implications for flat space holography.

papers.title_en: Transgression branes in seven dimensions
papers.abstract_en: A seven dimensional theory with branes, described by a Transgression Action is investigated. The theory has special properties owing to the factorization of the trace used to define the Transgression form. It is shown that in some cases the theory is similar to the models of branes proposed by Nepomechie, Wu and Zee as a higher dimensional generalization of models of particles with fractional statistics of Wilczek, Wu and Zee. Static Euclidean solutions are presented, and compared with similar solutions of Nepomechie,Wu and Zee. Then Lorentzian static solutions are considered, based in solutions of constant curvature black holes presented by Bañados and further studied by Guilleminot, Olea and Petrov. Topological phases and their implications for quantum statistics are discussed.

papers.title_en: Cylinder spectral curve and 1-cut Matrix model
papers.abstract_en: For a random matrix, with eigenvalues in a one-body potential $V(x)$ and a 2-body interaction $R(x,x')$, it is known that the resolvent converges in the large $N$ limit to an analytic function in the complex plane minus cuts, called the spectral curve. In the 1-cut case, a two-sheeted neighborhood of the cut is a cylinder with two simple ramification points. We describe these spectral curve data by boundary integral operators and generalized cycles. Vice-versa, given a 2-branchpoints spectral curve in a cylinder, there exists a formal random matrix model that corresponds to it. The goal of this article is to show the method to recover a formal random matrix model, with its potential and 2-body interaction, from the geometry of the spectral curve.

papers.title_en: Dynamical entropy on local causal horizons: the Einstein equation of state and canonical-energy flux
papers.abstract_en: For a twist-free null hypersurface, the Hollands-Wald-Zhang (HWZ) representative $S_{\rm loc}=(4G)^{-1}\int(1-Vθ)dA$, local on each cross-section (cut), obeys an exact off-shell Raychaudhuri identity with no term linear in the expansion, so no final equilibrium cut is needed. Given an entropy density $1/4G$, the Unruh temperature $κ/2π$ of an approximate local boost, local equilibrium cuts, and stress-tensor conservation, equating the leading equilibrium change of $S_{\rm loc}$ to matter boost heat yields $R_{kk}=8πGT_{kk}$ for every null direction, hence the Einstein equation with undetermined cosmological constant, an equation of state in Jacobson's conditional sense. On a fixed caustic-free generator bundle with $dA=J\,dA_{\rm ref}$, the functional $S_{\rm L}=(4G)^{-1}\int(1+\ln J-Vθ)dA_{\rm ref}$ obeys an exact balance per reference cell with curvature, shear, and expansion terms all positive, so under null convergence $S_{\rm L}$ is nondecreasing for $V\geq0$ until the first caustic. Conversely, requiring this balance for positive affine parameter on every small bundle and null direction is equivalent to the Einstein equation, given conservation and the stated normalization. Cut-locality, positivity, and first-order HWZ normalization select the density $1+\ln J-Vθ$ uniquely within a two-function class. Both functionals depend on the affine origin; we give their shift laws, identify the anchoring-invariant content, and show the origin is physical data fixed by the equilibrium cut. Near equilibrium, $S_{\rm L}$ agrees with the HWZ dynamical entropy at first order, and the temperature-weighted change of its Hessian equals the HWZ modified canonical-energy flux for stationary-vacuum perturbations. At finite amplitude, $S_{\rm L}$ is only a monotone geometric functional; reading it as entropy requires a coarse-graining postulate, stated but not derived.
publication_info: 58, General Relativity and Gravitation 58, 127 (2026), 127, publication, 2026, 127, Gen.Rel.Grav.

papers.title_en: Spectral function, OPE, and QNMs detect different singular points of black branes with unequal R-charges
papers.abstract_en: We consider black brane solutions in the STU model, with three R-charges labeled by the parameters $q_1,q_2,q_3$. For equal R-charges $q_1=q_2=q_3$, the solution becomes the Reissner-Nordström black brane. For unequal R-charges $q_1>q_2>q_3\geq0$, there are three curvature singular points at $R\equiv r^2=-q_i$. Only $R=-q_3$ is the physical singularity, and the other two lie beyond it. Their optical times $T_i$, the complex times of null rays from the boundary to these singular points and back, form a right triangle in the complex $T$-plane. We probe these singular points using three observables, all built from the retarded correlator of $T_{xy}$ at zero spatial momentum: spectral function, OPE coefficients, and QNMs. The exponentially small correction to the spectral function at large real frequency is dominated by $T_1$ and $T_2$, which have the smallest ${\rm Im}\,T_i$. The OPE convergence radius is determined by $T_1$, which has the smallest $|T_i|$. A line of QNMs lies along the direction of $1/T_2$, since $T_2$ has the smallest phase $\arg T_i$. Furthermore, there is a second line of QNMs along the negative imaginary axis, which carries information about $T_3$ corresponding to the physical singularity. We derive these results from a WKB analysis and check them numerically. The three observables are therefore sensitive to different singular points of the geometry.

papers.title_en: Superconductivity and Polar Metallicity in Atomically Thin Nitride Superlattices
papers.abstract_en: The integration of polar and superconducting materials in the atomically thin limit typically results in a competition that suppresses the superconducting order. Here, we challenge this conventional view by employing first-principles calculations to investigate 1:1 superlattices composed of alternating atomically thin layers of TiN/AlN and δ-NbN/AlN. Contrary to the expectation that dense insulating barriers would quench superconductivity, we find that the polar interface can coexist with a superconducting state. We observe that the transition temperature (Tc) of TiN is enhanced by nearly 2 K over its bulk value, while δ-NbN maintains a relatively high Tc exceeding 20 K. We demonstrate that this resilience arises from the formation of a polar metal, where the strong internal electric fields of the AlN layers are partially screened by a charge redistribution within the nitride layers. This screening mechanism, along with the geometric confinement, creates a quasi-two-dimensional electronic environment, establishing these superlattices as a novel platform for exploring the coexistence of structural inversion-symmetry breaking and superconductivity in the two-dimensional limit.

papers.title_en: Standalone Validation of a Pulsar Evolution Subroutine for NBODY6++GPU: Seven Test Scenarios
papers.abstract_en: Pulsars in globular clusters provide critical constraints on the evolution of compact objects. However, the treatment of neutron stars in standard N-body codes is outdated, and requires a better implementation of magnetic field decay, spin evolution, and accretion driven recycling that shape their observable properties. We present a standalone validation of a pulsar evolution subroutine for NBODY6++GPU, systematically tested across seven controlled scenarios prior to integration into full cluster simulations. These scenarios isolate distinct evolutionary regimes, including young pulsar spin down, millisecond pulsar weak torque evolution, accretion driven recycling in X-ray binaries, environmental torques in dense cores, wide binary systems, and compact binaries in the dipole spin-down regime. Through two separate numerical implementations, we achieve cross validation demonstrating better than 0.1% agreement across all physical quantities and timescales. Our validation confirms that analytical solutions are reproduced with high precision for isolated pulsars, gigayear scale evolution (tau_c ~ 1.0 Gyr) matches observations of millisecond pulsars in clusters like 47 Tucanae, and accretion driven recycling operates with physically realistic timescales, yielding a final period of 1.0 ms and a period derivative of approximately -5.9e-19 s/s, with accretion dominance by a factor of about 14. We demonstrate that environmental torques remain negligible even in the densest cluster environments, while compact binary spin down is validated; gravitational wave orbital decay is deferred to future work. All validation codes, test suites, and integration instructions are publicly available to support future applications.

papers.title_en: Thermodynamic, Optical, and Wave Signatures of Charged Letelier AdS Black Holes with PFDM and Quintessence
papers.abstract_en: We study a four-dimensional charged Letelier--anti-de Sitter (AdS) black-hole metric containing a cloud of strings, a phenomenological perfect-fluid-dark-matter (PFDM) source, and a Kiselev-type quintessence term. We derive the curvature invariants, horizon temperature, entropy, electric potential, and horizon-based mass function, and analyze local thermal response and the associated extended-phase-space identities. A rectangular benchmark cycle gives $W=0.095000$ and $η\simeq15.39\%$ for the explicitly stated geometric-unit parameters; these values are model- and cycle-specific and are not presented as a universal efficiency enhancement. For geometric optics, we derive the photon-sphere condition, critical impact parameter, and finite-radius shadow angle. For a massless, minimally coupled scalar field, we obtain a radial-coordinate Helmholtz equation and identify frequency-dependent barriers, evanescent intervals, and candidate trapping regions; the eikonal barrier-top scale approaches the photon-sphere capture scale. Two qualifications delimit the interpretation. First, with the stated PFDM stress-tensor convention, $ρ_{\rm PFDM}=-β/(8πr^3)$, so positive $β$ describes a negative-density effective source. Second, the mass function follows from the horizon equation, but identifying it with a conserved asymptotic AdS mass requires a separate charge and boundary-normalization analysis. The potential-well analysis likewise does not determine complex quasinormal frequencies. We therefore present the results as a consistent, parameter-specific analysis of the adopted phenomenological geometry, while distinguishing algebraic thermodynamic identities from conclusions requiring asymptotic-charge or spectral calculations.

papers.title_en: Deintercalation Equilibria Control the Composition, Structure, and Electronic Quality in the Synthesis of 2$M$-WS$_2$
papers.abstract_en: Alkali-metal intercalation-deintercalation (AMID) enables access to metastable layered materials such as 2$M$-WS$_2$. Mechanistic studies of AMID have focused on intercalation; how deintercalation proceeds and influences crystal properties is comparatively poorly understood. Here, we assess 34 deintercalation treatments of 2$M$-K$_x$WS$_2$ and find that K$^+$ removal proceeds through coupled redox and ion-exchange equilibria, whose positions set the composition, structure, and electronic quality of the products. Across a series of neat solvents, K$^+$ deintercalation amount increased with solvent polarity and was driven to near-completion upon addition of nonoxidizing crown ether chelators, regardless of solvent polarity. Spontaneous reintercalation occurred when 2$M$-WS$_2$ was placed in dilute aqueous solutions of the strong base KOH but not the neutral salt KCl. These results suggest that the extent of deintercalation is governed by the stability of K$^+$ in solution, rather than oxidant strength alone, consistent with a reaction under thermodynamic control. Treatments that bias the deintercalation equilibrium most strongly toward the products while avoiding deleterious side reactions produce the highest quality 2$M$-WS$_2$. A six-hour treatment with acidified K$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$ gave the highest average residual resistivity ratio ($\overline{RRR}$). Residual K$^+$, quantified by ICP-MS, was found in all treated samples and appeared to impose an upper bound on $\overline{RRR}$. Treatments yielding crystals with $\overline{RRR}$ below this bound did not always afford 2$M$-WS$_2$; we observed two new structures in bleach-treated samples and signatures of alternative phases under other conditions. This work demonstrates that deintercalation is not merely a processing step in AMID but a mechanistically rich reaction that might be rationally tuned to improve and control metastable materials.

papers.title_en: A No-Go Theorem for Order-Two Clifford Electric-Magnetic Duality
papers.abstract_en: Electromagnetic duality in the toric code has order two at the level of anyon types and acts as a Hadamard-type logical transformation on the encoded quantum information. Here, we ask whether it can likewise be realized microscopically as an order-two Clifford operation. For the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ toric code, we prove that any locality-preserving Clifford realization of electric-magnetic exchange cannot have order two. Our proof is fully general and requires neither translation symmetry with restricted families of system sizes nor a fixed pairing between vertex and plaquette stabilizers. Geometrically, the proof locally emulates the unavoidable crossing between electric and magnetic strings, similar to a cross-cap in a non-orientable manifold. Extending the problem to the $\mathbb{Z}_N$ toric code, we find that an order-two Clifford realization exists for odd $N$, whereas it is impossible for even $N$. Our result shows that the order-two exchange of closed-string operators cannot be extended to an order-two exchange of open-string operators.

papers.title_en: On the consistency of non-commutative geometry inspired Reissner-Nordström black hole solution
papers.abstract_en: We revisit the non-commutative geometry inspired Reissner-Nordström black hole solution obtained by smearing the point sources with a Gaussian distribution. We show that while the form of the metric function and the physical properties derived from that remain valid, not all the components of Einstein equations are satisfied: the angular components fail by exactly the Lorentz force density exerted by the electric field on the smeared charge, which the standard electromagnetic energy-momentum tensor leaves unbalanced. We construct an improved energy-momentum tensor that consistently satisfies Einstein equations. It is the unique conserved completion: the standard Maxwell tensor supplemented by an interaction stress supported on the smeared source. The improved tensor leads to a different prediction for the region where the strong energy condition is violated. For certain choice of parameters, our proposal predicts the violation of the energy condition outside the Cauchy horizon, which might be relevant for the stability of the inner horizon and strong cosmic censorship.

papers.title_en: Relative entropy of entanglement and tripartite minimal surface
papers.abstract_en: We propose a holographic dual of the relative entropy of entanglement for a boundary tripartition $A:B:C$. Our proposal is that, at the leading order, \begin{align} E_R(ρ_{AB}) = \frac{1}{4G_N}\Big[\mathrm{Area}(Γ_{\min}) - \mathrm{Area}(γ_{AB})\Big] \notag \end{align} where $Γ_{\min}$ is the minimal bulk tripartition surface and $γ_{AB}$ is the minimal surface homologous to $AB$. For a general random tensor network, we prove the corresponding upper bound by constructing a separable state associated with $Γ_{\min}$ and evaluating its relative entropy. We also establish the matching lower bound rigorously for networks of one, two, and three Haar random tensors by bounding the maximal tripartite product-state overlap. In appropriate geometries, the minimal tripartition surface can form a nontrivial tri-junction resembling the Mercedes logo.

papers.title_en: Trinity of Carrollian Gravity: Dynamically Equivalent Formulations of Magnetic Carrollian Gravity
papers.abstract_en: In this paper, we extend the paradigm of the Geometrical Trinity of Gravity to the Carrollian geometry to construct a comprehensive framework of dynamically equivalent theories for Magnetic Carrollian gravity. Utilizing the inherent ambiguities and freedoms of affine connections on degenerate metrics, we systematically relax the metric-compatibility and zero-torsion constraints of the rigid magnetic sector. By imposing global flatness on these modified connections, we prove that the curvature of a Magnetic Carrollian universe can be dynamically traded for isolated kinetic energy densities of torsion and non-metricity. Unlike the Lorentzian Trinity which maps gravity to alternative gravitational frameworks, the Carrollian equivalences can also map spacetime geometry to non-gravitational theories. Specifically, we demonstrate that intrinsic torsion recovers Electric Carrollian gravity as the Teleparallel equivalent of Magnetic Carroll gravity; purely spatial torsion reproduces kinetic terms stracturally similar to the magnetic Hamiltonian of scalar-charge Fracton gauge theory; and temporal torsion sectors map independently to $U(1)$ Maxwell electric fields and Carroll-Weyl conformal dilaton theories. Finally, by formulating a Symmetric Teleparallel Carroll connection with minimal non-metricity, we show that the Magnetic Carrollian Lagrangian is dynamically equivalent to an ultralocal, isotropic Electric Carrollian gravity upon exploiting the present freedoms in connection. These results establish a geometric dictionary translating Carrollian gravitational dynamics into the language of tensor gauge theories, electromagnetism, and dilaton theory.

papers.title_en: Stellar Disruption and Black Hole Retention in Massive Collisions: The Role of Thermonuclear Feedback
papers.abstract_en: A stellar-mass black hole (BH) that collides with a massive star can be captured by drag and settle at its center as a black hole star. Hydrodynamic simulations that neglect nuclear reactions have found that the star survives and becomes a black hole star (BH*) for BH-to-star mass ratios $q\lesssim0.2$. We perform hydrodynamic simulations of head-on collisions with the \athenak\ code, including CNO burning coupled to the gas, for $q=0.1$ and $0.2$ BHs, stellar masses of $100$ and $500\,M_{\odot}$, solar, metal-deficient, and Helium-rich compositions. In all models (with $q\le0.2$), the energy dissipated by drag is comparable to or less than the binding energy that the captured BH adds to the gas so that it alone does not disrupt the star. But, under compression around the captured BH, gas is heated to $\gtrsim2\times10^8$\,K and undergoes thermonuclear burning at the $β$-limited hot-CNO rate. Within about one dynamical time after the BH settles at the center, the nuclear energy released during the encounter becomes a significant fraction of the star's binding energy $\tfrac32\barβ\int P\,dV$. The star loses most of its mass once the cumulative release reaches this binding energy. Below this threshold, the release rate declines. Merger between a solar-composition star and a BH with a mass ratio $q=0.2$ leads to the disruption of the star after releasing most of its total mass. But a metal-poor star, with nearly the same binding energy and total yield, survives with minor release after merger with an identical BH. After coalescence with a less massive ($q=0.1$) BH, stars with both solar and metal-poor composition survive as black hole stars, burning at a rate $\gtrsim 10^{44}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$, far from thermal equilibrium. Very massive and helium-rich stars, which are weakly bound, are the most easily disrupted.

papers.title_en: Qubit representation of the mass observable in quantized Schwarzschild interior
papers.abstract_en: We develop a quantum-computational framework for the mass observable of the Wheeler--DeWitt quantized Schwarzschild black-hole interior. Working in the physical sector spanned by correlated two-mode oscillator states, we construct finite-dimensional representations of the mass operator and map them onto qubit operators through Pauli decomposition. We analyze the resulting representations for increasing truncation sizes and establish analytically the scaling of the number of nonvanishing Pauli terms and independent measurement settings. These results provide a quantitative characterization of the quantum resources required to encode and measure the black-hole mass observable. As a representative benchmark, we implement a two-qubit variational quantum eigensolver for the smallest nontrivial truncation and find excellent agreement with the exact finite-dimensional spectrum. We further describe a quantum-circuit procedure for verifying the Wheeler--DeWitt constraint independently of the mass estimation. Our results provide a direct connection between Wheeler--DeWitt quantum gravity and quantum computation and establish a structured route toward the quantum simulation of gravitational observables.

papers.title_en: Projections and topological classification of black hole thermodynamics
papers.abstract_en: Black hole thermodynamic topology has evolved from classifications based on global topological numbers to more refined schemes including boundary behavior. This development motivates a deeper question: how are different topological manifestations connected within the complete thermodynamic structure? In this paper, we propose the thermodynamic projection conjecture, which seeks to address this question by examining different topological manifestations in the context of the complete thermodynamic structure and exploring their underlying physical connections and formation mechanisms. As a representative application of this idea, we investigate temperature-dependent thermodynamic topological phase transitions, in which the topological number varies with temperature while the physical parameters are held fixed. We examine how the complete thermodynamic structure gives rise to different topological outcomes on different temperature slices. Our results demonstrate that temperature-dependent thermodynamic topological phase transitions arise from boundary effects, whereas the pairwise generation or annihilation of equilibrium states in the interior leaves the total topological number unchanged. These results establish that, at fixed physical parameters, the topological differences observed on different temperature slices originate from the same complete thermodynamic structure and can be understood within a unified framework of thermodynamic projections. Furthermore, this study offers a new approach to understanding black hole thermodynamic structures and their rich physical behavior through the interplay between global structures and their local manifestations.

papers.title_en: Untangling flow-harmonic correlations in OO and Pb--Pb collisions at the LHC using event-shape engineering
papers.abstract_en: Symmetric cumulants $\mathrm{SC}(m,n)$ measure the correlation between the event-by-event fluctuations of the flow harmonics $v_m$ and $v_n$, which, for higher harmonics, is influenced by the nonlinear response to the elliptic ($v_2$) and triangular ($v_3$) flow. Event-shape engineering, which selects events by the reduced flow vector $q_n$, is expected to control this contribution. However, its power is limited by the small forward multiplicity in light-ion collisions. In this work, we study the effect of the $q_2$ and $q_3$ selections on the symmetric cumulants in OO and Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.36$~TeV using EPOS4 with an ATLAS-like acceptance. Using the law of total covariance, the symmetric cumulant is separated into a selected part, which follows the differences between the $q_n$ classes, and a residual part within them. It is observed that in OO collisions the correlations of $v_2$ with $v_3$ and $v_4$ remain almost entirely within the $q_2$ classes, unlike in Pb--Pb collisions. Nevertheless, events with the smallest $q_2$ in central OO collisions show weaker correlations of $v_2$ with $v_3$ and $v_4$, which is attributed to $v_4$ approaching its linear response. In Pb--Pb collisions, the $q_2$ and $q_3$ selections act separately on the two factors of the nonlinear coupling of $v_5$, which establishes a way to isolate them experimentally.

papers.title_en: eAdS- embedded AdS, tensionless strings and contracted Carroll-Weyl symmetry
papers.abstract_en: We adapt the Dirac conformal $d+2$ dimensional embedding construction to define a null string in $AdS_{d+1}$. Introducing an extra Stückelberg field $\varphi$, which is a scalar under $AdS$ and shifts under local scaling of embedding space, the model acquires a local scaling invariance. We refer to this string as the embedded anti-De Sitter, $eAdS$, null string. A very useful property of this new gauged formulation is that, unlike previous gauged actions in $AdS$ background, the local scaling symmetry commutes with the $so(d,2)$ symmetry of $AdS$. Interestingly, the $eAdS$ null string is the tensionless limit of a tensile string in embedding space and the same holds for its reduction to an intrinsic description of AdS. We display the symmetries and constraint algebras both in embedding space and directly in AdS.

papers.title_en: Three-dimensional multipole states of the Bose-Einstein condensate of polar molecules in a shallow two-dimensional trapping potential
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the formation, stability, and dynamics of three-dimensional (3D) elongated multipole quantum droplets (QDs) in a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) of polar molecules with long-range interactions between molecular electric dipoles. The condensate is confined by a 2D trapping potential, which is a combination of the harmonic-oscillator potential and a central Gaussian potential hill. The system is modeled by an extended Gross-Pitaevskii (GP) equation, incorporating the dipole-dipole interactions and beyond-mean-field Lee-Huang-Yang (LHY) correction, which play a crucial role in stabilizing self-bound QD structures. In regimes of weak and strong confinement, stable multipole states with the number of lobes $n=2S$ are created by means of the imaginary-time-propagation (ITP) method from inputs with vorticity $S\leq 2$. The so created multipole QDs carry no angular momentum. Stable higher-order multipole states can be produced by the ITP method from inputs with $S\geq 3$ up to $S=6$ (i.e., $2S=12$ lobes) only under strong confinement and when the molecule number $N$ exceeds a threshold value. We analyze the dependence of the chemical potential, energy per particle, and peak density on $N$ and $S$ in the weak- and strong-confinement regimes. A noteworthy fact is that, below another threshold value of $N$, the minimum-energy (ground) state is created by the input with $S=1$, rather than $S=0$. Simulations of perturbed evolution reveal that, despite satisfying energetic stability criteria, only a subset of the multipole QDs are truly stable, with higher-order ones tending to develop instabilities or relax toward lower-order states. These results highlight the essential roles of the trapping potential, anisotropy of the dipole-dipole interactions, and LHY-induced repulsion in the formation and structural stability of multipole QDs.

papers.title_en: All Order Gravitational Wave Tails from Classical Soft Theorem for Subleading Post-Newtonian Expansion
papers.abstract_en: The low-frequency gravitational waveform emitted in a classical scattering process contains an infinite tower of late- and early-time tail terms of the form $u^{-r}(\ln|u|)^{r-1}$, $r \geq 1$. In the Newtonian limit, the coefficients of this entire tower have recently been shown to be universal, i.e. fixed by the asymptotic data of the scattering objects alone. At the retained order in the velocity expansion, these leading-logarithmic tails are determined to all orders in Newton's constant $G$. We extend this result to the first subleading order in the post-Newtonian expansion of the asymptotic states. We consider scattering of an arbitrary number of incoming and outgoing nonrelativistic objects interacting only through gravity at long range, and we derive the complete tower of tail terms at this order. The correction arises from the first subleading term in the retardation expansion and is determined by the asymptotic Newtonian trajectories of the massive particles. Its coefficients are again determined entirely by the asymptotic trajectories and are independent of the details of the interaction. For $2\to2$ scattering, the leading-logarithmic series can be summed in closed form. Our results agree with a relativistic conjecture proposed in earlier work arXiv:2610.07134.

papers.title_en: Time Running Backwards, and Where It Stops: Superoscillations of Proper Time and the Memory of the Environment
papers.abstract_en: A quantum system prepared in a superposition of proper times - a clock whose worldline is superposed, or a clock at rest in a superposed gravitational potential - evolves, in each branch, by the same dynamics for a different duration. Post-selecting the control that sets the proper time turns the superposition into a superoscillation of the time-dilation factor: the system is found to have evolved for a proper time $α_w t$, where the weak value $α_w$ may exceed unity, vanish, or be negative - the quantum time-translation machine of Aharonov, Anandan, Popescu and Vaidman. We ask how far back such a machine can run an irreversible process. The test system is a sealed cell - excited atoms, the radiation field they emit into, and the absorbing walls, carried as one quantum object - and the witness is projective: atoms that had begun to decay before the run are found, in the post-selected sub-ensemble, more excited than when inserted. The answer is exact and depends only on the atoms' survival amplitude. With two branches the witness holds only while the decay is younger than the memory time of the environment, after which the emission becomes Markovian. Beyond it, the post-selection amplifies the minute difference between the contents of the cell in the two branches, set by the full energy spread of the atoms and their field rather than by the linewidth, and the witness fails. Reversing a decay past the memory time requires many branches, an environment with a strictly bounded spectrum, and a post-selection probability that falls exponentially with the number of environmental oscillations to be undone. The obstacle to reversal is therefore not entropy but bandwidth - the same bandwidth that makes the emission irreversible in the first place. We give four ways to superpose a clock rate, from hollow massive shells to inertial velocities.

papers.title_en: A note on Positivity and Rigidity for an Expanding Quasi-Local Energy
papers.abstract_en: We study positivity and rigidity for an expanding quasi-local energy $E_λ$ associated with constantly umbilic initial data $(Ω,g,k=λg)$, introduced in earlier work [ALP26] as an analogue of the Brown-York energy adapted to an expanding flat de Sitter background. Under nonnegative scalar curvature and suitable boundary assumptions, our previous results established positivity for $λ$ below a geometrically determined threshold $α$, while vanishing $E_λ$ at $λ=α$ forced the boundary to be round. In this paper, we strengthen this endpoint rigidity statement by showing that, if $E_λ=0$ when $λ=α$, then $(Ω,g)$ is isometric to a closed Euclidean 3-ball of radius at most $1/λ$. The proof combines the rigidity theorem of Shi-Tam for the Brown-York energy with a strict concavity argument. We also construct an explicit counterexample to the positivity and rigidity conjecture formulated in [ALP26], showing that the energy can become negative beyond this threshold and that vanishing energy need not imply rigidity.

papers.title_en: $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes from the spectral edge of DSSYK and supersymmetric extensions
papers.abstract_en: The $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes of Do and Norbury are the top-degree parts of Okuyama's discrete volumes, which are defined by topological recursion on the spectral curve of the double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model. We show that the same $q$-deformed volumes can also be obtained from a double-scaled matrix model whose disk density is found by zooming in on the soft edges of the DSSYK density. Applying the same procedure to the hard edge of $\mathcal{N}=1$ DSSYK, we obtain candidate $q$-deformed $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes. They are polynomials of fixed degree, and they reduce to $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes in a scaled $q\to1$ limit. These candidate volumes differ from the $\mathcal{N}=1$ volumes of Do and Norbury in (arXiv:2510.12431) up to what we call ``irrelevant'' contributions which exactly vanish in the scaled $q\to 1$ limit. Together, these results demonstrate how $q$-deformed volumes can be naturally associated to the spectral edges of various DSSYK models and provides an intuitive way to construct them in supersymmetric contexts.

papers.title_en: Multilayer Heater Nano cryotrons: Electrothermal Modeling of Geometry-Dependent Switching
papers.abstract_en: This paper presents a finite-element framework to study how device geometry affects the switching current of multilayer heater nano cryotrons (hTrons). The device comprises a 50 nm Au/5 nm Ti heater, a 100 nm SiO2 spacer, a 23.6 nm NbN channel, and a Si substrate. Two-dimensional electrothermal simulations examine nine heater and channel width combinations using widths of 100, 500, and 1000 nm. Three-dimensional simulations show how heat flows through the layers and spreads across the channel near the heater-channel overlap. Heater electrical losses and heat transport are coupled, whereas the channel switching threshold is obtained separately from a temperature-dependent constitutive relation. Published global temperature measurements support the switching-law calibration, and heater-current measurements assess the resulting device response. The model measurement comparisons show a systematic reduction of switching-current density with heating, but also geometry-dependent discrepancies in the low-drive plateau and transition shape. A common extraction protocol is formulated for heater-current and heater-power requirements at a specified suppression level, while separating fitted device amplitudes from controlled geometry effects. The resulting comparisons connect thermal fields to design metrics while distinguishing calibration from validation and excluding transient-performance claims from the stationary analysis

papers.title_en: Loss-Cone-Limited Dark Matter Capture by Early Black Hole Seeds
papers.abstract_en: The rapid appearance of supermassive black holes at high redshift motivates a reassessment of non-baryonic growth channels. We develop a new loss-cone framework for collisionless dark-matter (DM) capture by early black-hole seeds, with particular attention to phase-space depletion and refilling. The calculation combines Eddington-inverted NFW-like halos, a relativistic direct-capture boundary, and an orbit-averaged Fokker-Planck treatment of angular-momentum transport. Primordial black holes (PBHs) are treated as massive perturbers whose refilling strength depends on both their abundance and individual mass. Collisionless refilling by triaxial or chaotic centrophilic orbits is included as a phenomenological upper-envelope channel. We show that ordinary stellar relaxation gives negligible DM-driven growth for the fiducial high-redshift seeds. PBH-driven granularity can yield order-of-magnitude growth in sufficiently compact halos, while triaxial or full-loss-cone supply can produce a rapid early burst. In the self-consistent calculations, however, the evolution generally becomes supply-limited. Once the accessible low-angular-momentum phase-space reservoir is depleted, the capture rate collapses and the black-hole mass saturates. Fixed-background NFW calculations therefore overestimate sustained growth, especially in the full-loss-cone limit. A TNG50-calibrated NFW benchmark gives negligible growth even under optimistic refilling assumptions. Collisionless DM capture is therefore unlikely to solve early SMBH growth in generic NFW-like halos, but it can provide a radiatively dark upper envelope in rare compact environments with efficient angular-momentum refilling.

papers.title_en: Two-peak gravitational wave spectra from supercooled two-field phase transitions
papers.abstract_en: We study the gravitational wave (GW) spectrum generated by supercooled first-order phase transitions in two-field conformal models. We construct three representative toy models that capture the essential features of these models, derive analytical criteria for the existence of two-step transitions, and show how the two-field dynamics generate a genuine two-peak GW spectrum. We identify regions of parameter space in which two-peak GW spectra are observable at LISA and the Einstein Telescope. By way of illustration, we apply our analysis to a realistic conformal dark SU(3) model.

papers.title_en: Energy Extraction via Magnetic Reconnection from a Rotating Dyonic Black Hole in $N = 2, \ U(1)^2$ Gauged Supergravity
papers.abstract_en: We study energy extraction via magnetic reconnection from a rotating dyonic black hole in four-dimensional $N=2$, $U(1)^2$ gauged supergravity. Using the Comisso-Asenjo mechanism in the ZAMO frame, we derive the asymptotic hydrodynamic energy per unit enthalpy $ε^{\infty}_\pm$ and determine when reconnection outflows attained negative energy at infinity. By varying the spin $a$, electric and magnetic charges, NUT parameter $N_g$, and gauge coupling $g$, we compute the cutoff magnetization $σ_0^{\rm cutoff}$ and map the region of parameter space that admits $ε^{\infty}_-<0$. We find that $σ_0^{\rm cutoff}$ and the very existence of Comisso-Asenjo extraction are tightly controlled by $g$ and the dyonic charges: increasing $g$ or pushing the charges toward extremality raises $σ_0^{\rm cutoff}$ and shrinks the CA-active part of the ergoregion. Unlike Kerr, the spin enters through the normalization factor $Ξ$, and the quartic horizon function $Δ_g$, so geometric effects from the AdS/NUT deformation dominate the usual frame-dragging enhancement. As a result, the extracted power and efficiency are non-monotonic in $a$ and peak at intermediate spin ($a\sim0.8$); near-extremal rotation is not required for high efficiency, provided $g$ is small and $Q$ is moderate. Efficient extraction further demands extreme magnetization and nearly radial outflows, confining the active reconnection layer to a thin shell, just outside the horizon.

papers.title_en: Monodromy Defects and Bulk Renormalization Group Flows on the Fuzzy Sphere
papers.abstract_en: A monodromy around a defect specifies a symmetry transformation, but the low energy properties of the defect depend on its interaction with bulk degrees of freedom and also itself. We study this dependence on the fuzzy sphere. Along an anisotropy flow, an $O(3)$ half-twist approaches the $O(2)$ half-twist when its twisted components stay light and disappears when they become massive. At large $N$, untwisted spectators give a positive correction to the defect entropy, fixed by the conformal weight of the free defect. The surviving $O(2)$ monodromy admits a relevant charged perturbation that pins the line. Pinning before or after the easy-plane bulk flow gives matching infrared junction data. A pin of the untwisted component survives only the opposite, easy-axis flow. Walls between opposite pinnings test the stability of the candidate ordered line. They are relevant on the pinned $O(2)$ monodromy lines studied and favoured to be relevant, with a smaller margin, on the ordinary $O(2)$ line, while the ordinary $O(3)$ and $O(4)$ walls lie close to marginality. We separate the wall dimension into a tilt stiffness and an angular shape, comparing them with a Ward identity, a two-loop expansion and a large-$N$ saddle. In the fully twisted large-$N$ model, winding weakens the condensate and lowers the wall dimension and the entropy released by pinning. The resulting entropy comparison permits disordering into the unpinned line wherever the leading wall estimate is relevant. Finally, we construct the regular half-twist on the fuzzy four-sphere as a starting point for analogous questions in five dimensions.

papers.title_en: Self-Interacting Dark Matter: From Particle Physics Theories to Structure Formation Simulations
papers.abstract_en: We establish a unified theory-to-simulation framework for self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) that integrates three components: (i) a comprehensive, self-contained treatment of its particle-physics foundations and a broad range of model classes; (ii) a systematic, quantitative mapping from microscopic dark-sector physics to structure-formation simulation inputs through explicit expressions and numerical prescriptions; and (iii) the development, implementation, and validation of a broad suite of SIDM algorithms and a dedicated DM decay module in the moving-mesh code AREPO-2. Under (i), we detail the particle content, symmetries, interactions, production mechanisms, and constraints of a broad landscape of elementary and composite SIDM models, and present representative viable benchmark models. Under (ii), the mapping specifies cosmological initial conditions, internal-state masses and populations, reaction networks, velocity- and angle-dependent cross sections, dissipative energy loss, and decay rates and recoil kinematics. We then apply this mapping to a broad range of SIDM model classes. Under (iii), we implement and validate SIDM algorithms with constant and velocity-dependent cross sections, covering isotropic and anisotropic scattering, multi-state elastic and inelastic reactions, and dissipative processes, alongside a dedicated DM decay module in AREPO-2. We validate the implementations through beam-lattice deflection, thermalization and decay tests, isolated-halo gravothermal core-collapse simulations, and cosmological box and zoom-in simulations. The results recover analytical predictions and published benchmarks and demonstrate agreement across numerical schemes. Our theory-to-simulation framework serves as a cross-disciplinary reference and a practical bridge between SIDM particle physics and simulations of nonlinear structure formation.

papers.title_en: Variational Approach to the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon Equations of Motion for Extended Objects in General Relativity
papers.abstract_en: The exact motion of a finite size object in curved spacetime is captured by the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon equations. They associate a unique worldline, momentum, and spin to that object and determine the evolution of such in terms of its fully independent multipole moments. We provide a thorough review of this theory and show how to build it directly via a manifestly gauge invariant variational principle well-suited for effective descriptions of relativistic compact objects. We discuss conditions under which the covariant spin supplementary condition can be enforced and identify the natural basis of curvature tensors conjugate to the object's multipole moments.

papers.title_en: The Energy-Momentum Tensor of a Compact Object in General Relativity to all Multipole Orders
papers.abstract_en: In effective field theory approaches to compact object motion in general relativity, spin and tidal effects are encoded by operators formed from the Riemann tensor and its derivatives. Many such operators contribute degenerately to observables, with a single one often affecting several multipole moments of the body. Using the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon formalism, we construct a natural basis of independent tensors which are each canonically conjugate to precisely one multipole. We find the novel exact distributional formula for the energy-momentum tensor of a compact object in terms of its reduced multipole moments and these tensors.

papers.title_en: Radial Oscillations of Viscous Stars at Finite Temperature
papers.abstract_en: We study the radial oscillation spectrum of relativistic stars within Israel-Stewart and Navier-Stokes theories, extending previous analyses to include heat diffusion and a thermodynamically consistent finite-temperature equation of state. The inclusion of heat flux gives rise to a distinct thermal sector in the mode spectrum, whose structure closely mirrors the dispersion relations of an infinite dissipative fluid. Within Israel-Stewart theory, the thermal modes transition from purely damped to propagating behavior above a critical overtone number, providing a finite-size realization of relativistic second sound in compact stars. Remarkably, the finite stellar geometry can push even the fundamental thermal mode into the propagating regime -- a feature with no continuum analogue. For the class of equations of state considered here, where finite-temperature corrections enter as controlled, Sommerfeld-type perturbations of a cold polytrope, the thermal sector couples only weakly to the ordinary fluid oscillation spectrum, with the coupling being of second order in a suitable temperature parameter. We further show that the discrete stellar spectrum is well captured by an analytic ansatz constructed from the flat-spacetime dispersion relations, with the star's finite radius discretizing the continuous mode structure. Our results complete the analysis of radial oscillations of viscous stars by incorporating the last remaining dissipative degree of freedom within the Israel-Stewart framework.

papers.title_en: A constrained mixed variational formulation with Legendre-dual defects for incremental irreversible thermodynamics
papers.abstract_en: We present a constrained mixed variational formulation for incremental irreversible thermodynamics. A single augmented action combines a linearized contact-increment penalty, equilibrium and dissipative Fenchel--Young defects, a storage--transport functional, and multipliers enforcing the constitutive increments. Under frozen-coefficient and boundary assumptions, stationarity yields the linearized contact condition, the Tisza relation, the Onsager flux--force law, and the implicit balance equation. An exact-elimination theorem shows that the contact and multiplier fields can be reconstructed algebraically from a solution of the reduced weak balance problem. We also prove off-shell invariance of the equilibrium--storage--multiplier sector under an equilibrium-sector partial Legendre transformation; invariance of the full augmented action is not claimed. For Fourier heat conduction, we derive a weighted drift identity and a per-step energy-drift bound for the energy-representation three-term incremental functional. In one spatial dimension, a small-time-step estimate yields a uniform $H^1$ bound and a discrete $L^2(0,T_f;H^2)$ bound, leading to cumulative $O(δt)$ drift over fixed time intervals. A conservative mixed discontinuous Galerkin (DG0)--Raviart--Thomas (RT0) discretization with fully implicit conductivity $κ(T)=1+T^2$ preserves discrete energy to roundoff. A separate lumped-mass piecewise-linear benchmark reproduces the predicted finite-step drift.

papers.title_en: Stochastic Acceleration Downstream of Astrophysical Shocks
papers.abstract_en: Generation and evolution of turbulence at shock fronts are crucial aspects of the process of particle acceleration in different classes of sources. Here we aim at describing the fate of non-thermal particles and turbulence in the downstream region of an astrophysical shock, both in the case in which turbulence is solely produced upstream and advected through the shock and in the case in which additional turbulence is injected downstream. In particular we will provide an estimate of the effect of stochastic acceleration on particles accelerated at the shock and then advected behind it. The calculations will be specialized to supernova remnant shocks. The temporal evolution of the particle distribution function downstream of the shock and the power spectrum of the turbulent perturbations are both followed by solving numerically the transport equations for the two quantities, accounting for the damping of waves due to the particles that resonantly interact with them, which makes the problem non-linear. Our calculations show that, if waves are only self-generated upstream via Bell instability, they are not able to significantly modify the particle spectrum in the downstream region. Additionally, turbulent cascading in $k$-space quickly drains their energy, further limiting the stochastic acceleration of particles. If, on the other hand, there are additional sources of turbulence downstream, then these waves can contribute meaningfully to second order Fermi acceleration and alter the spectrum of particles. This may reflect in the spectrum of gamma radiation produced through $pp$ scattering downstream. Although second order Fermi acceleration is typically slower than diffusive shock acceleration, particles are expected to stay downstream of shocks for much longer times during which stochastic acceleration can modify their spectrum and affect the spectra of multi-messenger emissions.

papers.title_en: Configurational Information and Hadron Spectroscopy in Holographic QCD
papers.abstract_en: Based on the concepts of entropy and complexity, Configurational Information Measures (CIMs) are tools capable of extracting information regarding physical systems from their spatially localized energy density, determining properties such as stability limits and phase transitions. In this thesis, CIMs are employed to investigate hadron spectroscopy. By utilizing phenomenological AdS/QCD models in conjunction with CIMs, cataloged meson and baryon resonances are interpolated into structures analogous to Regge trajectories, from which analytical expressions are derived to estimate the masses of higher-order excited states. These estimates are compared with experimental data to search for possible correspondences that may elucidate the properties of particles that have been experimentally detected but remain unidentified. Using this CIM-based AdS/QCD hybrid method, this work analyzes light mesons within a dynamical model, strange vector kaons in a framework that accounts for constituent quark masses, and light-flavor baryons at finite temperature.

papers.title_en: Breathing mode of quantum droplets in dipolar quantum gases: A sum-rule analysis
papers.abstract_en: We investigate theoretically the ground-state properties and breathing-mode collective excitations of three-dimensional dipolar Bose gases in anisotropic harmonic traps incorporating quantum fluctuations. Combining a Gaussian variational ansatz with a sum-rule analysis, we derive explicit analytical expressions for both axial and radial breathing-mode frequencies, which are validated by numerical solutions of the time-dependent extended Gross-Pitaevskii equation. Our theoretical predictions show great agreement with existing experimental data for $^{166}$Er and $^{162}$Dy gases. By constructing comprehensive phase diagrams across the parameter space of the $s$-wave scattering length, atom number, and trap aspect ratio, we reveal both discontinuous first-order phase transitions and smooth crossovers between the dilute Bose-Einstein condensate and dense quantum droplet phases. We confirm that the enhanced incompressibility induced by quantum fluctuations significantly elevates the breathing-mode frequencies in the droplet phase compared with conventional weakly interacting Bose gases. Furthermore, the system undergoes a phase transition and a crossover over the scattering length under the elongated and flattened confinements, characterized by discontinuous jumps and continuous crossovers in peak density and atomic cloud sizes, respectively. Our work offers a useful analytical framework to characterize collective excitations in dipolar quantum gases, providing quantitative insights for forthcoming ultracold atom experiments in lanthanide atoms and polar molecules.

papers.title_en: Pair size versus coherence length and quantum geometry in the spin-orbit coupled BCS-BEC crossover
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the interplay between pairing correlations and quantum geometry in the spin-orbit-coupled BCS-BEC crossover. Working in the helicity basis, we derive the exact pair-size tensor for the two-body bound states and show that it separates into an intraband contribution and a quantum-geometric interband contribution governed by the quantum metric. We extend this decomposition to two distinct many-body length scales at zero temperature: the Cooper-pair size from mean-field BCS theory and the coherence length from Gaussian fluctuation theory. Although the two almost coincide in the BCS regime, the former measures the internal extent of a pair while the latter measures the long-wavelength response of the order parameter. Evaluating both for three-dimensional Rashba, three-dimensional Weyl, and two-dimensional Rashba spin-orbit couplings, we find that the pair size decreases monotonically with spin-orbit coupling, whereas the coherence length develops a pronounced minimum, associated with the collapse of the noninteracting Fermi surface onto the ring or sphere of helicity-band minima, before growing again as the composite bosons become weakly interacting. The quantum-geometric contributions reach up to about 30\% of the squared pair size and squared coherence length, tracking the same changes in the helicity Fermi-surface topology.

papers.title_en: Massive Scalar Quasinormal Modes and Quasibound States of Charged Black Holes with Logarithmic corrections
papers.abstract_en: We study how long-range deformations in a black-hole metric affect the oscillation, trapping, and decay of a neutral, minimally coupled massive scalar field. We choose a logarithmic deformation of Reissner-Nordström (RN) sourced by nonlinear electrodynamics, arising as an exact solution of Einstein gravity. The same geometry also arises in a phenomenological perfect-fluid dark-matter model. We provide several exact completions of this geometry with finite Arnowitt-Deser-Misner (ADM) mass. Focusing on the original logarithmic geometry, we analyze both quasinormal modes (QNMs), which describe relaxation, and quasibound states (QBSs), which describe trapped modes with small horizon absorption. We first show that a small scalar mass moves the potential barrier outward, raises it, and reduces its curvature. First-order WKB then predicts weaker damping at every fixed finite multipole and overtone. We then compare several approaches, namely sixth-order WKB, global matching, a generalized Leaver method (adapted to the logarithmic geometry) and time-domain evolution. All methods yield consistent QNM estimates within their ranges of validity. Global matching and Leaver also agree closely for QBSs. Further analytic estimates with a reference trapped state show that a local Padé approximation gives a binding-energy error of about $0.04\%$, while leading Gamow tunnelling underestimates damping by about $25\%$. Across the sampled QBSs, increasing the scalar mass or nonlinear coupling strengthens binding but shortens the lifetime through greater horizon absorption. Finally, using an appropriate horizon regularization and a common complex radial contour, we demonstrate orthogonality of an independently computed QNM-QBS pair using a suitable relativistic bilinear framework.

papers.title_en: Klein bottle ratio of two-dimensional ferromagnetic Potts models
papers.abstract_en: The weakly first-order nature of the two-dimensional five-state ferromagnetic Potts model poses challenges for numerical study. Using density-matrix and tensor-network renormalization group methods, we investigate these transitions of the $q$-state Potts model via the Klein bottle ratio $g$ on original and dual lattices. Finite-size scaling of $g$ as a function of transverse system size $L_y$ accurately locates the critical points for $q = 3, 4, 5, 6$. We further examine the transfer-matrix spectra and entanglement entropy, extracting central charges through toroidal and Klein bottle boundary conditions. For $q = 5$, the extracted central charge ($c \approx 1.14811$) is close to the real part of the theoretical value $c_{5\text{-Potts}} = 1.1375 \pm 0.0211 i$ predicted by complex conformal field theories(CFTs). The observed drift in the scaling exponent $b$ effectively distinguishes the continuous transition from the weakly first-order regime. Furthermore, the extrapolated divergence of $g$ confirms the first-order character of the $q=5$ Potts model, while for the $q=4$ model, both the CFT-predicted eigenvalue distribution and the logarithmic corrections are numerically verified.

papers.title_en: Probing the origin of the LHAASO Peanut with a hidden central accelerator
papers.abstract_en: A highly asymmetric, giant Peanut-shaped structure has been detected by the Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO) in ultra-high-energy gamma rays at high Galactic latitude, $b\approx-17.5^{\circ}$, suggesting anisotropic particle transport around a Galactic accelerator. We investigate whether its spectrum and morphology can arise from a hidden central accelerator embedded in a projected anisotropic halo. The baseline model accounts for the diffuse strip and central excess, while a phenomenological prescription for a localized magnetic field reorientation toward the line of sight (LOS), together with a particle-conserved remapping of the electrons downstream of the far excess into an emitting column of prescribed transverse extent, enhances the emission at the far excess position. We explore various source ages, along with different combinations of ambient magnetic field strength and parallel diffusion coefficient, while accounting for radiative cooling when estimating the viewing geometry. The exploration reveals that relatively rapid parallel transport enhances the far component while preserving a dominant diffuse strip. Representative configurations remain compatible with the observed spectral energy distribution, although the fitted far component remains comparatively weaker than the central component above 100 TeV, even in cases where their component fluxes are comparable at 25-100 TeV. These results illustrate the plausibility of a hidden central accelerator as the origin of the LHAASO Peanut, while identifying the remaining difficulty in reproducing the relative brightness of its compact components within the adopted phenomenological framework.

papers.title_en: Charge-Activated Birefringence and Shadow Mimicry around Reissner-Nordström Black Holes
papers.abstract_en: We discover that electric charge can activates birefringence for a neutral vector field coupled to the Einstein tensor around a Reissner-Nordström black hole. Changing the electric charge of an uncoupled black hole can mimic one parity's shadow radius of a coupled black hole. The coupling makes the two parity looks differently. It separates their shadow edges of two parities and produces a backward-scattered signal with reversed helicity. However changing the charge alone cannot reproduce both effects. They require both nonzero charge and coupling. At weak coupling, the leading correction is the same for both potential. Positive coupling raises the potential, reduces low-frequency absorption and decrease the average shadow radius. Negative coupling reverses these trends. The backward signal is nonzero, this is due to the difference between the complex scattering amplitudes of the two parities. It is entirely helicity reversed. For the uncoupled field, the shadows is the same for both parities and the backward intensity vanishes exactly at every charge. We can use the split edge and backward signal to distinguish the coupling from a change of charge alone. A comparison with observations still requires a mechanism that produces and detects this field.

papers.title_en: Sub-Thouless energy scale in interface-dominated unconventional superconductor junctions
papers.abstract_en: We derive the conductance in unconventional superconductor - normal metal - normal metal junctions, taking into account the resistance between the normal metals. We show that applying Tanaka--Nazarov boundary conditions at both superconductor and normal metal interfaces reveals a new characteristic low-energy scale which is sub-Thouless in the experimentally relevant strong-interface regime. This scale governs, among other quantities, the curvature of the local density of states (LDOS) and the width of conductance dips near the zero-bias conductance peak in triplet superconductor junctions, thereby replacing the Thouless energy as the dominant low-energy parameter. We derive universal $s$-wave proximitized diffusive metal expressions for the zero-bias LDOS and differential conductance which solely depend on the interface and bulk resistances, independent of the superconducting gap and Thouless energy scale. This framework provides a possible origin of the anomalous low-bias conductance features observed in unconventional superconductors, offering a refined mechanism for interpreting interface and correlated electron physics in experimental hybrid junctions.

papers.title_en: Identifying Contributions to the Superconducting Diode Effect through Nonreciprocal Superconducting Properties
papers.abstract_en: Nonreciprocal superconducting responses provide a sensitive probe of superconducting states in systems where inversion and time-reversal symmetries are broken. However, in the superconducting diode effect (SDE), where the critical current differs for opposite current directions, nonreciprocity can also arise from vortex-induced contributions caused by minute magnetic field misalignment, complicating its interpretation. Here, we investigate a noncentrosymmetric $[Nb/V/Ta]_{40}$ superlattice and demonstrate nonreciprocity in all three fundamental superconducting properties: the critical current, critical field, and superconducting transition temperature. By measuring the angular dependence of the nonreciprocal critical field $ΔB_{\mathrm{c} 2}$, we separate the contribution of misalignment-induced out-of-plane vortices from the in-plane response. We identify a sharply enhanced SDE emerging near $B_{\mathrm{c} 2}$, accompanied by nonreciprocal responses in $T_{\mathrm{c}}$. These observations exhibit phenomenology similar to that reported in layered superconductors, where an orbital-FFLO state with finite-momentum Cooper pairing has been reported. Our results establish a protocol for assessing out-of-plane vortex contributions to the superconducting diode effect and demonstrate that nonreciprocal responses provide complementary probes of unconventional superconducting states.

papers.title_en: Quadrature magnetoresistance scaling reflects linear field dependence rather than strange metallicity of high-temperature superconductors
papers.abstract_en: The quadrature scaling of magnetoresistance has been widely adopted as a hallmark of the strange metal state. However, whether this scaling signals quantum criticality or reflects conventional transport behavior remains controversial. Here, by systematically investigating the magnetotransport properties of NiTe2 nanosheets, we demonstrate that the quadrature scaling is not a unique signature of strange metallicity. We find that the scaling holds only when the crossover field Bc, marking the transition from quadratic to linear magnetoresistance, is sufficiently small relative to the applied field range. Through controlled simulations, we show that the scaling emerges whenever linear magnetoresistance dominates, irrespective of its origin, and fails when the linear regime is inaccessible. This conclusion is supported by observations in SrTiO3 based heterostructures, where quadrature scaling appears despite the absence of strange metal behavior. Our results establish that the quadrature scaling merely reflects the presence of linear magneto resistance, urging caution in using this scaling as a diagnostic tool for exploring the strange metal state.

papers.title_en: Self-bound quantum dark fermion stars: saturation, a coupling-capped maximum mass, and tidal signatures of a vector dark sector
papers.abstract_en: I show that a dark sector whose fermions couple to both a scalar and a vector mediator saturates in close analogy with nuclear matter: the energy per particle develops a minimum at finite density, cold dark matter of this kind is self-bound, and its stars, computed here in full general relativity, possess the sharp surfaces of strange quark stars. Saturation makes the maximum stellar mass a property of the Lagrangian rather than an inheritance of the Chandrasekhar scaling: it rises eightfold across the saturation window, which a critical vector coupling closes, so the theory caps its own maximum mass, at $3.9\,M_\odot$ for a fermion of $1\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and the fiducial saturation density, a ceiling shared by the whole family of couplings rather than by any single parameter set. Metastable couplings support two disconnected stable families, one dilute and gravitationally bound, the other dense and self-bound. The quantum-pressure correction, confined by saturation to a surface layer a few Compton wavelengths thick, governs the smallest dark nuggets whilst shifting stellar masses by less than one part in $10^{21}$. A $1.4\,M_\odot$ member of the fiducial family has a radius of $13.3\,\mathrm{km}$, a compactness of $0.155$, and a tidal deformability of $1.6\times 10^{3}$, almost an order of magnitude above the measured neutron-star value, so at a given particle mass and couplings a single well-measured inspiral distinguishes these stars from neutron stars and from their scalar-only counterparts, whilst the deformability surviving at the maximum mass separates them, in principle, from black holes.

papers.title_en: Black-hole ringdown at an exceptional point
papers.abstract_en: Black holes ring in damped oscillations. At an exceptional point, photon-sphere and near-horizon modes merge, and their response can acquire a linear time factor. We compute its amplitude from constrained Einstein-Maxwell data for a rotating, charged black hole in de Sitter space. With seven competing modes fixed, the late-time curvature error is 0.00383$\%$ for the pair and 0.01401$\%$ for a refitted exponential. We suppress the linear term by tuning the initial disturbance at fixed geometry. Hence, near coalescence, changing only the initial disturbance can shift the frequency inferred from a short ringdown fit.

papers.title_en: Strong Collective Dynamics Hidden behind a Nearly Free Single-Particle Spectrum
papers.abstract_en: Single-particle spectroscopy has long served as a criterion for the strength of electronic correlations: strong collective motion is expected to shift and broaden spectral peaks and to renormalize the dispersion. Here we show that this correspondence can fail on the same microscopic orbital. The mechanism relies on local interference between two resonant side orbitals: one suppresses low-energy real transitions into the interacting environment, while the other suppresses spectral-weight backflow to the source orbital; virtual mixing nevertheless transfers the environmental spin polarization to the source. We prove a rigorous relative spectral bound that is uniform in environment size and interaction strength and holds for arbitrary stationary states; the protection becomes stronger as the relative frequency resolution improves. In a fully quantum two-cell device, a collective mode softens by 60%, whereas the particle intensity at the free peak changes by only 3.6 parts per million. Quantum Monte Carlo shows that the transferred spin response grows with spatial correlations and is quantitatively predicted by the free-band polarization. These results recast the meaning of a simple particle spectrum and provide a design principle for quantum probes that combine predictable particle spectra with strong collective sensitivity.

papers.title_en: Axion Quality in Warped Extra-Dimension
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the axion quality problem in warped extra-dimensional models in which the QCD axion arises as the Wilson-line mode of a five-dimensional $U(1)$ gauge field compactified on an $S^1/\mathbb{Z}_2$ orbifold. Higher-dimensional gauge invariance severely constrains possible sources of Peccei--Quinn symmetry breaking, implying that non-QCD contributions to the axion potential are predominantly generated by nonlocal effects mediated by $U(1)$-charged fields propagating along the compact dimension. We systematically compute these contributions and examine how both the warped geometry and the orbifold fixed points (branes) affect the resulting axion quality. Finally, we classify the parametric suppression of the induced axion potential, thereby identifying the conditions under which warped extra-dimensional axions can achieve sufficiently high quality.

papers.title_en: Ferromagnetic resonance signatures of edge states for distinguishing chiral and helical $p$-wave superconductors
papers.abstract_en: We theoretically investigate ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) modulation at interfaces between ferromagnetic insulators and two-dimensional chiral and helical $p$-wave superconductors. We evaluate the surface dynamical spin susceptibility, including both edge and bulk quasiparticle excitations. For momentum-conserving interfacial exchange at zero temperature, the edge contribution to the Gilbert damping exhibits distinct frequency scalings for the excitation energies well above the spectral broadening, $\hbarω\gg2δ$: $δ/(\hbarω)^{2}$ for the chiral state and $1/\hbarω$ for the helical state. For a clean superconducting boundary, edge-induced Ising spin anisotropy persists even when interfacial exchange disorder randomizes momentum transfer. The low-energy edge response is suppressed when the magnetization aligns with the edge-state spin axis. These results establish FMR modulation as a probe complementary to existing methods for distinguishing the chiral and helical states and constraining their $d$-vector directions.

papers.title_en: Scalar-tensor reconstruction of coherent quantum black holes
papers.abstract_en: We construct a scalar-tensor realisation of spherically symmetric black hole geometries that effectively arise from quantum coherent states characterised by a finite core and finite extension. We determine the non-minimal coupling to the Einstein-Hilbert Lagrangian, kinetic coupling, and scalar potential and show that the kinetic term is positive only in finite domains. For fixed black hole mass, the boundaries of these domains provide a natural mechanism that relates the core size and spatial extension to the dynamics of the scalar-tensor realisation. We further show that the same geometry can also be obtained from a Horndeski action with derivative coupling and determine its domain of validity. Neither reconstruction includes the event horizon nor can it simultaneously reproduce arbitrarily large portions of the interior and exterior of the black hole, whose quantum origin therefore appears to remain partially outside the regime of applicability of semiclassical theories of gravity.

papers.title_en: Generalized Second Law of Thermodynamics in $f(Q)$ Symmetric Teleparallel Gravity
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the validity of the generalized second law (GSL) of thermodynamics on the cosmological apparent horizon in $f(Q)$ symmetric teleparallel gravity, using the Wald-type entropy prefactor $Af_Q/4G$ together with a correction term derived directly from the modified Friedmann equations. We derive, and verify by explicit symbolic computation, a closed-form expression for the apparent horizon entropy in $f(Q)$ gravity and show that its time derivative combines with the matter entropy rate into a remarkably compact master formula, $T_A\dot S_{\rm tot} = 4π\dot H(\dot H f_Q + H\dot f_Q)/H^4$ (in units $8πG=1$), which correctly reduces to the known general-relativistic limit. We apply this formalism to three observationally viable $f(Q)$ models --- power-law, exponential, and logarithmic. We find that the GSL is satisfied throughout cosmic history for all three models, and relate this robustness to a general, theory-independent structural condition: for ordinary pressureless matter obeying the null energy condition, GSL validity reduces to the sign of $\dot H$, i.e., to the absence of a phantom crossing in the total effective expansion history. The geometric sector exhibits model-dependent energy conditions, power-law and exponential models violate only the strong condition, while the logarithmic model violates the null, weak, and dominant conditions for \(z>-1\), and the strong condition for \(z<3.84\).

papers.title_en: Superconductivity beyond band geometry: emergence of pair quantum geometry
papers.abstract_en: The quantum geometry of Bloch states is known to shape the effective mass of single particles in multiband systems. We show that this connection extends to paired states. For a multiband Hubbard model with on-site attraction, we derive an exact effective-mass theorem for two-body bound states in vacuum and its counterpart for Cooper pairs near the critical temperature within Gaussian fluctuation theory. In both cases, the inverse mass contains, besides a ``conventional'' term from band dispersion and band geometry, a distinct term governed by a quantum metric on the manifold of paired states. This pair-geometric term requires a sublattice pairing texture that varies with the pair momentum and, like the band quantum metric, depends on the orbital embedding, whereas the total mass does not. The one-body, two-body, and Cooper-pair theorems follow from a single construction, with the band mass recovered as a special case. When a collective mode lies inside the two-particle continuum, its continuation to the second Riemann sheet renders the fluctuation kernel non-Hermitian, leading to a biorthogonal quantum geometry and a complex Cooper-pair mass whose real and imaginary parts describe propagation and damping. Exact calculations for the sawtooth, Su-Schrieffer-Heeger, Hofstadter, and fluorite-like lattices show that pair geometry contributes significantly to the mass of bound pairs, and the fluorite-like lattice exhibits both an undamped Cooper pair with a real mass and a damped one with a complex mass. Pair quantum geometry thus emerges as an essential ingredient of multiband superconductivity beyond band geometry.

papers.title_en: Constraining Cosmic Deceleration using the Solar System
papers.abstract_en: We investigate whether Solar System dynamics can provide independent constraints on the present day cosmological deceleration parameter $q_0$, offering a complementary approach to conventional cosmological probes. By relating cosmic acceleration to a weak Hooke type radial perturbation, we derive bounds using planetary perihelion precession, trans-Neptunian objects, and Oort cloud dynamics. We obtain relatively robust planetary bounds of $|q_0|\lesssim 10^9$, while the outer Solar System yields potentially stronger, albeit more model dependent, constraints approaching $10^5$. Through Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation and sensitivity analyses, we explore the statistical robustness of these estimates and their dependence on orbital measurements. Finally, we demonstrate how future precision astrometry and outer planet missions could improve these limits by several orders of magnitude, establishing Solar System dynamics as a complementary laboratory for probing cosmological acceleration.

papers.title_en: ERG, axions, and a PT-symmetric accelerating Universe
papers.abstract_en: In conventional quantum mechanics, the Hamiltonian is required to be Hermitian, ensuring real energy eigenvalues. Certain non-Hermitian Hamiltonians can also possess entirely real spectra when they are invariant under the combined action of parity ($\mathcal P$) and time reversal ($\mathcal T$). Such Hamiltonians are called unbroken parity--time ($\mathcal{PT}$)-symmetric. We conjecture that, in a string-inspired scenario, a repulsive phase of gravity may be due to a $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric gravitational theory, characterised by anomalous Chern-Simons terms, coupled to axion fields. The conjecture is based on the behaviour of the chiral anomalous couplings of these axions to electromagnetic potentials. Within the Exact Renormalisation Group (ERG) framework in the modified local potential approximation, we argue that singularities in the ERG beta functions for such couplings may indicate an infrared phase transition. At the energy scales of these singularities, we conjecture that the field theory transitions from the Hermitian phase to a ${\mathcal P}{\mathcal T}$-- symmetric theory, of gravity, characterised by a repulsive Netwon's ``constant''. This may induce the acceleration observed in the Universe at late eras, without the need for a dark--energy component.

papers.title_en: Integrals of motion for the deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$
papers.abstract_en: The deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$ of type $D_l$ possesses an infinite family of commuting elements that can be viewed as a two-parameter deformation of the classical Hamiltonians for the KdV hierarchy of type $D_l$; these conserved charges are termed local integrals of motion (IMs). Concurrently, the quantum toroidal algebra $U_q(D_l^{"})$ of type $D_l$ admits four distinct representations via free field realizations, each corresponding to one of the four end nodes of the affine Dynkin diagram. Utilizing these representations, we associate an infinite set of commuting operators with each node, which we define as non-local integrals of motion. Both local and non-local integrals of motion act simultaneously on a shared Fock space consisting of $l+1$ free fields. We provide a direct, computational proof demonstrating that these local and non-local integrals of motion mutually commute.

papers.title_en: SMMAN studies of AGN variability. II. Radio and optical quasi-periodic oscillations and changing variability states in the relativistic jet of the blazar PKS 0754+100
papers.abstract_en: We report the detection of $\sim$280-day quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in the SMMAN observations of PKS 0754+100 at 4.8 and 23.6 GHz, which may also be present in VLBI observations made at 15 GHz. The onset of a transition of the amplitude of variability in the radio flux density, observed more clearly in the 15 GHz and 23.6 GHz observations, coincides with the detection of a likely QPO of $\sim$1.4 days in optical observations made by the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite. This transition in radio variability also occurs close in time to the disappearance of the secondary knot in the VLBI radio map during the lower variability state. An X-ray flare was observed 100 days before this transition, suggesting that the mechanisms causing these quasi-periodicities are related. After the transition to a higher variability state, both the 15 and 23.6 GHz light curves exhibit indications of QPOs at $\sim$400 days. For the first time, a QPO detected in the radio band from a BL Lac has been seen to appear to shift to a QPO of lower frequency, with that transition occurring near the appearance of a QPO in optical emission at a much shorter period.
